title: Verbs in -ir and -re
topic: present tense of regular -ir (finir) and -re (attendre) verbs
why: After the -er verbs, here are the two other regular groups: finir and its -iss- plural, and attendre with its silent d. With them, you can describe errands and habits, and avoid the classic traps of attendre (no “for”) and entendre (to hear, not to intend).

{"lessons": ["

Verbs like finir: the -iss- group

After the -er verbs, French has a second regular group: verbs in -ir like finir (to finish). Their secret is a little -iss- that appears in the plural.

finir (to finish)choisir (to choose)réfléchir (to think)
jeje finisje choisisje réfléchis
tutu finistu choisistu réfléchis
il, elle, onil finitelle choisiton réfléchit
nousnous finissonsnous choisissonsnous réfléchissons
vousvous finissezvous choisissezvous réfléchissez
ils, ellesils finissentelles choisissentils réfléchissent

The singular endings are -is, -is, -it, and all three sound the same: “fee-nee”. The plural adds -iss- before the endings you know (-ons, -ez, -ent). So the plural is where you hear the difference: il finit (“fee-nee”) / ils finissent (“fee-neess”). The -ent is silent, as always, but the double s is heard.

Other common verbs on this pattern: réussir (to succeed, to pass), grandir (to grow up), remplir (to fill, to fill in).

Je finis le travail à dix-huit heures, mais Paul et Léa finissent à vingt heures.I finish work at six p.m., but Paul and Léa finish at eight.

Not every verb in -ir follows this pattern. Partir, sortir and dormir have no -iss- and come in unit 3: for now, the verbs of this lesson are your models.

", "

Verbs like attendre: the -re group

The third regular group ends in -re: attendre (to wait for), vendre (to sell), répondre (to answer). Take off -re: the stem ends in a d, and that d is silent in the singular.

attendre (to wait for)répondre (to answer)perdre (to lose)
je / j'j'attendsje répondsje perds
tutu attendstu répondstu perds
il, elle, onil attendelle répondon perd
nousnous attendonsnous répondonsnous perdons
vousvous attendezvous répondezvous perdez
ils, ellesils attendentelles répondentils perdent

Two things to notice. With il / elle, there is no ending at all: il attend, elle répond, and the d is silent. And again, the plural reveals the consonant: il attend (“a-tan”) / ils attendent (“a-tand”). Listen for that final d to tell singular from plural.

Other verbs on this pattern: vendre (to sell), entendre (to hear), descendre (to go down, to get off).

Le boulanger vend des croissants. Les clients attendent devant la boulangerie.The baker sells croissants. The customers are waiting outside the bakery.

The singular of -re verbs and -ir verbs ends in -s, -s, -t / -d: je finis, tu finis, il finit; j'attends, tu attends, il attend. When you write il, check the last letter.

", "

English traps and daily errands

These verbs hide a few traps for English speakers, all about little words:

FrenchEnglishwatch out
attendre le busto wait for the busno preposition: never “attendre pour”
répondre à Paul, répondre à la questionto answer Paul, to answer the questionFrench needs à
entendreto hearfalse friend: not “to intend”
réussir un examento pass an examnot “to succeed an exam”
choisirto choose, to pickje choisis un gâteau

Note that à + le becomes au: je réponds au professeur. Take it as it is for now: these contractions are explained in unit 3.

At the shops

With these verbs, you can describe your errands and habits:

Je descends à la boulangerie. J'attends un peu, puis je choisis un pain.I go down to the bakery. I wait a little, then I choose a loaf.
Vous vendez des livres ? — Non, désolé, ici, c'est une boulangerie ! La librairie est dans la rue.Do you sell books? — No, sorry, this is a bakery! The bookstore is down the street.
Les enfants grandissent vite et ils remplissent le panier !The children are growing up fast and they're filling the basket!

And another false friend in passing: la librairie is a bookstore, not a library (la bibliothèque).

Réfléchir means “to think it over”, before deciding: Je réfléchis = Let me think. It's not about mirrors!
